title: How many tiles will Step n of the square tile pattern need?
description: A pattern of square tiles forms a ring round a square hole. The tiles are counted as a big square take away the hole, and again as four rows plus four corners, and both counts are shown equal. Keeko doubts the count when the four corner tiles are left out.
teaching_notes: One idea: a ring of tiles is a big square take away a hole, and a second way of counting must give the same expression. Watch for students who count only the four sides and leave out the corner tiles.

source: The tile pattern has 8, 12 and 16 tiles in its first three s
video_script.why: The child has seen two counts of a circle pattern agree, and now does the same for a ring of square tiles with a hole.
video_script.substitution: See Step n as a square of side n plus two with a square hole of side n, multiply out, and check with a second count.
video_script.anchor: the pattern of square tiles of the book, Steps one, two and three, each a ring of tiles round a square hole
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts four sides of ten tiles each and says Step ten has forty tiles, leaving out the four corner tiles.
video_script.payoff_line: Step n has four n plus four tiles

final_answer.value: Step 4 has 20 tiles, Step 10 has 44, Step n has (n + 2)² − n² = 4n + 4
final_answer.spoken: Step four has twenty tiles, Step ten has forty four, Step n has four n plus four

maths_rules: Step n: a square of side n + 2 with a square hole of side n, so (n + 2)² − n²
second count: 4 rows of n tiles plus 4 corner tiles, 4 × n + 4 = 4n + 4
slip: 4 × 10 = 40 leaves out the 4 corners; Step 1 would be 4 × 1 = 4, not 8
video_script.design: One idea: a ring of tiles is a big square take away a hole, and a second count agrees. Wrong idea: four sides only, no corners. The tile ring stays all video; the working board holds the algebra.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a pattern of square tiles.
<bookmark mark='steps'/>Step one has eight tiles, Step two has twelve, and Step three has sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We want the tiles in Step four, Step ten and Step n.
Can you see how the tiles are arranged in each step?

beats.on_screen: the tile steps hold still on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Step 1 drawn as a 3 by 3 square with the middle tile as a hole; Step 2 as a 4 by 4 square with a 2 by 2 hole; the hole is shaded in a pale colour in each

marks.ring: each step is outlined as a ring of tiles round a hole
marks.one: Step 1 shows a 3 by 3 square with one hole tile
marks.two: Step 2 shows a 4 by 4 square with a 2 by 2 hole
marks.side: the side of the hole is labelled n and the side of the whole square n + 2

beats.colours: the hole in a pale colour, the tiles in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='ring'/>Look at the tiles. Each step is a ring of tiles round a square hole.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one is three by three, with one tile missing in the middle.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two is four by four, with a hole of two by two.
<bookmark mark='side'/>In Step n the hole has side n. The ring adds one tile on each side, so the whole square has side n plus two.

beats.on_screen: Given: Step 1 has 8, Step 2 has 12, Step 3 has 16 tiles

marks.given: the three counts are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Step one has eight tiles, Step two has twelve, and Step three has sixteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: tiles in Step 4, Step 10 and Step n

marks.find: the three things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the tiles in Step four, Step ten and Step n.

beats.on_screen: whole square side n + 2, hole side n; tiles = (n + 2)² − n²

marks.whole: the whole square of side n + 2 and the hole of side n are labelled

beats.colours: the whole square and the hole in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>First, the whole square has side n plus two, and the hole has side n.
<bookmark mark='tiles'/>The tiles are the whole square take away the hole. That is n plus two, all squared, take away n squared.

marks.mul: (n + 2)(n + 2) is written with its four small products
marks.join: the two middle products join into 4n, giving n² + 4n + 4

beats.colours: the two middle products in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Second, multiply out n plus two by itself. That is n times n, plus n times two, plus two times n, plus two times two.
<bookmark mark='join'/>The middle parts join into four n, giving n squared plus four n plus four.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>Take away n squared, and four n plus four is left.

beats.on_screen: second count: 4 rows of n tiles + 4 corner tiles = 4 × n + 4 = 4n + 4

marks.rows: the four sides of n tiles glow, one on each side
marks.corner: the four corner tiles glow in another colour

beats.colours: the sides in one colour, the corners in another
narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Third, count another way. Four sides of n tiles make four times n.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>The four corner tiles add four more.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Four times n plus four is again four n plus four, so the two ways agree.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>Fourth, put in the step numbers. Step four is four times four plus four, which is sixteen plus four.
<bookmark mark='s10'/>Step ten is four times ten plus four, which is forty plus four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Step n has (n + 2)² − n² = 4n + 4 tiles; Step 4 has 20 tiles, Step 10 has 44

marks.ans: Step n has 4n + 4 tiles is boxed
marks.nums: Step 4 has 20 tiles and Step 10 has 44 are written under the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Step n has four n plus four tiles.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Step four has twenty tiles, and Step ten has forty four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the tile steps
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: Step 10 = 4 × 10 = 40, struck out; Step 1 beside it: 4 × 1 = 4 but Step 1 has 8 tiles; the 4 corner tiles of Step 1 glow

marks.test: Step 1 appears with 4 × 1 = 4 beside its 8 tiles
marks.fix: the four corner tiles of Step 1 glow
marks.plus: 40 + 4 = 44 is written and 40 is crossed out

beats.colours: the wrong idea in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Step ten has forty tiles, because each of the four sides has ten tiles.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test that on Step one. Four times one is four, but Step one has eight tiles.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The four corner tiles belong to no side, so they were left out.
<bookmark mark='plus'/>Add them back, and Step ten has forty plus four, which is forty four.
